context.brief:
## Employee
- Name: Gandu (no id)
- Role: Instrumentation Engineer, Instrumentation
- Plant / unit: Haldia  / Unit 300

## Equipment history in the knowledge graph
- none found for this profile; interview from the profile alone and ask them to name their key equipment

topics.title: Unit 300 Instrumentation Landscape – Key Equipment & Unwritten Quirks
topics.rationale: No equipment is recorded in the knowledge graph for this profile. The interview must start by having Gandu name the critical instruments he owns.
seed_questions: Which 5-10 instruments or control loops in Unit 300 would you say are most critical to safety or uptime?
For each one, what is the one undocumented quirk or workaround that keeps it running?
Are there any instruments that everyone is afraid to touch because only you know the calibration trick?

topics.title: Undocumented Instrument Failure Patterns & Early-Warning Signs
topics.rationale: Capturing the subtle, unwritten signs of impending failure that Gandu has learned over decades before they appear in any logbook.
seed_questions: What are the early-warning signs you listen for, smell, or feel during rounds that tell you a transmitter or valve is about to fail?
Which instruments fail in ways that the DCS trend never captures?
What is the biggest 'gotcha' in Unit 300 that nobody has ever written down in a procedure?

topics.title: Role Evolution & Unwritten Responsibilities
topics.rationale: Understanding the gap between Gandu's official Instrumentation Engineer title and the actual scope of work he performed, including tasks he absorbed unofficially.
seed_questions: How has your role changed since you started in Unit 300, and what responsibilities did you take on that were never in your job description?
What tasks do you handle today that you think management doesn't realize are part of your workload?
If you had to write a 'shadow manual' for your job, what would the first chapter be?

topics.title: Vendor & Contractor Tribal Knowledge
topics.rationale: Identifying the specific vendor representatives, local suppliers, or contractors who are essential to solving problems but whose names aren't in any system.
seed_questions: Who are the specific vendor reps or local technicians you call when you have a tricky problem—the ones who actually know the equipment?
Are there any vendors or spare parts that have become obsolete, and what is your secret workaround to keep those instruments running?
Which contractor or third-party shop does the best calibration work that the official procurement process might overlook?

topics.title: Half-Finished Projects & Abandoned Modifications
topics.rationale: Uncovering instrumentation projects that were started but never fully commissioned, which may pose a risk or represent sunk cost.
seed_questions: Are there any instrumentation upgrade projects in Unit 300 that were started but never finished?
What is the current state of those half-finished installations—are they bypassed, partially wired, or sitting in a box?
What would be the first step to either complete or safely decommission those abandoned modifications?

topics.title: Critical Control Loop Tuning & Mental Notes
topics.rationale: Capturing the specific PID tuning parameters, valve positions, or manual overrides that Gandu keeps in his head and are not saved in the DCS or documentation.
seed_questions: Which control loops in Unit 300 are currently running on manual or with tuning parameters that only exist in your head?
Are there any loops where the 'official' tuning parameters in the DCS are wrong, and you use a different set of values?
What is the one loop you worry will become unstable within a week of your departure?

topics.title: Safety Instrumented System (SIS) & Interlock Bypass History
topics.rationale: Documenting the informal history of safety system bypasses, testing anomalies, and the 'real' reason certain trips occurred.
seed_questions: Can you walk me through the history of any SIS or critical alarm bypasses that were managed informally or had recurring nuisance trips?
What is the most unreliable safety sensor in the unit, and how have you managed that risk?
Are there any interlocks that you know have a delayed response time that isn't reflected in the functional test records?

topics.title: Spare Parts Scarcity & Improvised Solutions
topics.rationale: Identifying critical instrumentation that is no longer supported by the manufacturer and the improvised solutions Gandu uses to bridge the gap.
seed_questions: Which instruments in Unit 300 are obsolete, and what is your 'jugaad' or improvised fix to keep them running?
Where are the hidden stashes of critical spare parts that only you know about?
If a specific obsolete transmitter fails on a Sunday night, what is the step-by-step workaround you would use that isn't in the manual?

topics.title: Startup & Shutdown Instrumentation Anomalies
topics.rationale: Capturing the transient instrument behaviors during plant startup and shutdown that are not captured in standard operating procedures.
seed_questions: During a Unit 300 startup, which instruments typically give false readings until the process stabilizes?
What is the manual sequence of valve overrides you perform during a trip that isn't written in the emergency procedure?
Are there any specific ambient weather conditions (monsoon, extreme heat) that cause specific instruments to drift, and how do you compensate?

topics.title: Successor Advice & Open Risks
topics.rationale: Providing direct advice to the incoming engineer about the biggest risks and the first things they should check.
seed_questions: If you had 30 minutes to brief your replacement, what are the top 3 risks you would tell them to monitor immediately?
What is the one piece of equipment you recommend they physically inspect on their very first day?
What is the 'skeleton in the closet' of Unit 300 instrumentation that they need to know about but won't find in any report?

topics.title: Unwritten Calibration & Maintenance Shortcuts
topics.rationale: Documenting the efficient, field-proven methods Gandu uses that deviate from the official manual but are essential for keeping the plant online.
seed_questions: What calibration steps in the official manual do you always skip or modify because they don't work in the field?
Are there any specific tools or homemade jigs you use for instrument maintenance that a new person wouldn't find in the workshop?
What is the 'trick' to getting an accurate zero on the difficult pressure transmitters in this unit?

topics.title: Interpersonal & Cross-Functional Dependencies
topics.rationale: Mapping the informal network of operators, process engineers, and managers that Gandu relies on to get instrumentation work approved or executed.
seed_questions: Which operators in Unit 300 have the best 'feel' for the process and give you the most reliable feedback on instrument performance?
Who in the process or mechanical team do you rely on to get things done quickly, outside of the formal work order system?
Are there any historical conflicts or communication breakdowns between instrumentation and other departments that your successor should be aware of?
